question: Does the first Essays agent-runtime vertical include a capability-bounded WebAssembly extension host?
selected_option: Require a capability-bounded WebAssembly component host in the first vertical, with its engine, WIT world, WASI target, resource budgets, cancellation, evidence, and denied ambient capabilities frozen through subsequent decisions.
rationale: The user explicitly selected OPT-WASM-FIRST-VERTICAL-HOST. This makes portable extension isolation part of the bounded first construction campaign while preserving the Rust daemon as the only Essays semantic authority.

required_semantics: the first vertical includes a WebAssembly component host behind a versioned typed extension interface
extensions consume immutable or revision-bound context and return proposals, diagnostics, or evidence; they never mutate accepted Essays state directly
the host exposes no ambient filesystem, process, shell, environment, secret, credential, network, database, browser-driver, or publication authority
every host import is explicitly declared, capability-bound, resource-bounded, revocable, and recorded
component identity, digest, interface version, granted capabilities, inputs, outputs, limits, cancellation, and outcome are evidence-bound
memory, table, instance, transferred-data, execution, concurrency, output, and wall-time limits fail closed
guest traps, timeouts, cancellation, malformed output, unavailable imports, and host failures cannot partially mutate accepted state
the native Rust daemon remains the sole accepted-state semantic authority and revalidates every extension proposal
non_implications: WebAssembly does not replace the native Rust daemon, Tauri desktop shell, canonical protocol, or supervised browser driver
sandboxing does not make extension code trusted or grant it Essays authority
this posture does not select an engine, WIT world, WASI release, SDK, component registry, signing scheme, cache, or numeric resource budget
this selection does not authorize dependency installation, implementation, component execution, browser effects, publication, release, or deployment
this selection does not prove isolation, determinism, portability, performance, compatibility, or conformance

remaining_blockers: WebAssembly engine and component ABI baseline
WebAssembly host capabilities, resource budgets, cancellation, component identity, and evidence rules
Essays security-owner review of the remote authentication binding
remote capability authorization and grant semantics
Product Capability decision and dependent contracts
authored ontology closure and DomainSpec generation
